holder: The people claiming belief in what was sent down to the addressee and before him, while wanting judgment from the taghut.
proposition: That they have believed in what was sent down to the addressee and in what was sent down before him.
scope_note: The outer أَلَمْ تَرَ asks about seeing these people; their claiming is positively attributed within its relative clause. The negation governs seeing, not claiming.
truth_evidence: 4:60 contrasts the profession with يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَحَاكَمُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَقَدْ أُمِرُوٓا۟ أَن يَكْفُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ; 4:61 names the people turning away as ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ. Their profession is presented as insincere.
note: Held records the claim attributed to them, without assuming they inwardly believe their own profession.

holder: Those who differed concerning him or the matter of his killing.
proposition: That they killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary.
scope_note: إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ positively attributes following supposition. The preceding مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ negates knowledge, not their following supposition.
truth_evidence: 4:157: وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ. 4:158: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ.
grounds_evidence: 4:157: مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ expressly denies knowledge of the matter.
unsure: proposition: The noun has no expressed complement. The killing claim is recovered from the same verse, but the differing people may entertain incompatible accounts.
alternative: The noun can cover the differing parties' unspecified opinions rather than only the killing claim. Then the proposition is unspecified and truth is open for those opinions as a set; the denial of knowledge remains.
note: The target is in the text's response to the quoted killing claim, not within that quotation. No reconstruction of what was made to appear is supplied.

holder: The children of Israel described in 5:70 as rejecting some messengers and killing others.
scope_note: وَحَسِبُوٓا۟ positively reports the attitude. The negation in أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ is inside the proposition.
truth_evidence: 5:71 follows the expectation with فَعَمُوا۟ وَصَمُّوا۟ ثُمَّ تَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُوا۟ وَصَمُّوا۟ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ. I read this adverse sequel of failure and divine turning as correcting their expectation of no trial.
unsure: truth: The sequel corrects the expectation by implication; it does not expressly say that a trial occurred.
alternative: If blindness and deafness describe only their conduct rather than a trial or its result, truth should be open.
note: The kind of trial is left unspecified. Rejecting messengers identifies conduct, but is not stated as evidence on which they based this expectation.

holder: The people addressed as asking who will restore them and when it will happen.
proposition: That they had remained only a little while.
scope_note: I read 17:52 as continuing قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا in 17:51. إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا restricts duration inside the proposition; it is not a condition or a negation of thinking.
unsure: reporter: The time clause can continue the instructed answer or resume direct narration.
scope: Instructed-speech scope depends on continuing the final command to say in 17:51.
proposition: The window does not expressly identify the interval during which they remained.
alternative: If 17:52 resumes the text's own address, reporter becomes text and scope plain. The stay may be the interval before resurrection, but its starting point is not specified here.
note: The call and response are predicted, while the accuracy of their estimate of elapsed time is not separately assessed.

holder: The addressees who invoke others apart from Him.
proposition: That those invoked apart from God have power to relieve or redirect their harm.
scope_note: قُلِ introduces the instruction containing ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ. The prior claim is positively attributed inside it.
truth_evidence: The instructed answer in 17:56 says فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ ٱلضُّرِّ عَنكُمْ وَلَا تَحْوِيلًا. The text continues in 17:57 that the invoked beings themselves يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ.
unsure: proposition: The claiming verb's complement is elliptical; power to relieve harm is recovered from the immediate challenge and denial.
alternative: The complement may be broader: that those invoked are gods apart from Him. Falsity then follows from their lack of power and dependence on their own Lord.
note: The command to invoke them does not make the earlier claim hypothetical. Content is recovered only from this passage.

reporter_who: The people saying in 17:90 that they will not believe the messenger until their demands are met.
holder: The messenger addressed as you, to whom the quoted speakers attribute the claim.
proposition: That the sky will be brought down upon them in pieces.
scope_note: وَقَالُوا۟ in 17:90 opens the quotation. كَمَا زَعَمْتَ in 17:92 attributes an earlier claim to its addressee. حَتَّىٰ in 17:90 conditions their professed willingness to believe on fulfillment of their demands; it does not condition the attributed earlier claiming.
unsure: proposition: The earlier claim is not quoted; a prediction, conditional warning, or claim of ability are possible.
alternative: They may attribute a claim that he can cause the sky to fall, or a warning that it could fall under some condition. That changes the proposition to a capacity or conditional warning; truth remains open here.
note: The text reports the challengers' attribution without independently reproducing or endorsing the alleged earlier statement.

scope_note: فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ introduces Pharaoh's words; إِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ affirms his attitude within them.
truth_evidence: 17:101 introduces the encounter with وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ, presenting clear signs from God. In 17:103 the narrator acts against Pharaoh: فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا. I read that framing as rejecting Pharaoh's diagnosis.
unsure: truth: The narrative discredits the accusation by implication, without separately saying that Moses was not bewitched.
alternative: If bewitched is treated as a narrowly literal condition not settled by the divine source of the signs, truth can remain open. Moses' rebuttal alone is a quotation, not independent narrative endorsement.
note: The signs are the setting, but no observation or argument is explicitly identified as Pharaoh's relied-on ground.

proposition: That Pharaoh is doomed to destruction.
scope_note: قَالَ introduces the reply to Pharaoh in 17:102; وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ affirms the attitude within that reply.
truth_evidence: The text's narration in 17:103 states فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا, realizing Pharaoh's destruction.
unsure: grounds: The preceding assertion about Pharaoh's knowledge of the signs can function as an implicit reason for the verdict, but is not expressly presented as what Moses relies on.
alternative: If لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرَ in 17:102 is read as the stated premise of the verdict, grounds becomes stated, with that clause as evidence.
note: The subsequent destruction establishes truth; it is not evidence Moses is said to possess beforehand.

holder: The people addressed as believers in 33:9, during the arrival of the armies.
proposition: The contents and polarities of their thoughts about God are not specified.
scope_note: وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ reports their thoughts during the remembered situation introduced by إِذْ جَآءُوكُم. The temporal setting is not a conditional case.
grounds_evidence: 33:10 supplies the immediate stimulus: إِذْ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ, followed by وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ. These are threatening circumstances prompting the thoughts, not a stated proof.
unsure: proposition: The plural noun supplies no one content or polarity. The quotation in 33:12 belongs to a subset, not automatically everyone addressed.
grounds: Attack and fear are the stated setting and stimulus; no explicit phrase says the holders treated them as evidence.
alternative: On a narrower definition of relied-on grounds, the circumstances are only the occasion and grounds becomes not reported. Restricting the thought to 33:12 would make the proposition that God and His messenger promised only delusion, while narrowing the holder to the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts.
note: The verb and cognate noun describe one attitude. I do not assign a single subset's opinion to the entire addressed group.

holder: The obstructers and people calling their brothers away, described in 33:18-19 as fearful and not believing.
proposition: That the confederate armies have not departed.
scope_note: يَحْسَبُونَ positively reports the attitude; لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا۟ negates departure within its proposition. The following وَإِن يَأْتِ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ conditions their subsequent wish, not this attitude report.
truth_evidence: 33:25 narrates وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنَالُوا۟ خَيْرًا وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلْقِتَالَ. Alongside the possible renewed arrival in 33:20, this presents the armies as already repelled.
note: Additional context requested and read with print-sura: 33:23-25, to check the narrated outcome instead of supplying it from memory. Fear in 33:19 is not expressly identified as evidence on which this belief rested.

proposition: That he would obtain their following.
scope_note: وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ reports realization of his expectation without negation, question, or condition governing the attitude.
truth_evidence: 34:20 states صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ, explicitly confirming the expectation through their following, with an exception.
unsure: proposition: The original expectation is not quoted. Its content is recovered from its realization; the exact extent originally expected is unstated.
alternative: If the expectation is reconstructed as everyone following without exception, the believers' exception qualifies its realization, and unqualified truth=true would not fit that universal proposition. Universality has not been inserted into the primary proposition.
note: 34:21 denies his authority over them, not expressly his knowledge or evidence for this expectation. No statement of Iblis from another sura is used.

holder: The addressees who invoke others apart from God.
proposition: That those invoked apart from God possess divine power or a share in it.
scope_note: قُلِ introduces the instructed challenge ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ. It positively attributes their prior claim.
truth_evidence: 34:22 denies possession with لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, and partnership or assistance with وَمَا لَهُمْ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرْكٍ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْهُم مِّن ظَهِيرٍ, in the answer the text commands.
unsure: proposition: The claiming verb's complement is elliptical; power or a share in it is recovered from the immediate denials.
alternative: The complement can be broader: that those invoked are gods apart from God. Falsity then concerns divine status and follows from the same denials.
note: The denials concern the invoked beings' powers, not expressly the holders' knowledge or proof. They are not classified as a denial of grounds.

holder: Those in whose hearts is sickness.
proposition: That God will not bring out their grudges.
scope_note: أَمْ حَسِبَ puts the positive attitude in a question. لَّن negates God's bringing out their grudges inside the proposition, not the attitude.
truth_evidence: 47:30 promises وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِى لَحْنِ ٱلْقَوْلِ, making their recognition through their manner of speech certain, instead of their hostility staying permanently hidden.
unsure: attitude: Held records the positive attitude being challenged; the question can instead be left open as an assertion of an actually entertained belief.
alternative: If attitude only records independently asserted holding, attitude becomes open; the interrogative scope and negative proposition remain.
note: Falsity rests on the promised disclosure in the following verse, not on the question alone.

holder: The hypocritical men and women and the associating men and women described here.
proposition: The content of their adverse thought about God is not specified in this clause.
scope_note: ٱلظَّآنِّينَ بِٱللَّهِ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوْءِ positively describes the groups. وَيُعَذِّبَ continues the purpose construction from 48:5 without negating or questioning their thinking.
unsure: proposition: Adverse or evil qualifies the thought without giving a complete proposition or its polarity.
truth: The thought and holders are condemned, but this window does not determine the truth of an unspecified proposition.
holder_kind: The definite group labels can identify groups in this address or describe those categories generally.
alternative: If the group labels are categories generally, holder_kind becomes generic and scope also includes generic or hypothetical. Taking the thought as a prediction against God's support of believers requires more specific content than this window states.
note: The participle and cognate noun describe one attitude. Moral censure alone has not been treated as a truth value for an unstated proposition.

holder: The Arabs left behind, addressed in the answer to their excuse in 48:11.
proposition: That the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families.
scope_note: بَلْ ظَنَنتُمْ continues, on this reading, the answer introduced by قُلْ in 48:11. أَن لَّن يَنقَلِبَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِيهِمْ أَبَدًا is a negative proposition under a positive attitude. The earlier question in 48:11 does not govern this corrective assertion.
unsure: reporter: 48:12 may continue the instructed response or resume direct narration.
scope: Instructed-speech scope depends on continuing the command from 48:11.
truth: The expectation is censured, but this window does not explicitly narrate the return needed to directly contradict its content.
grounds: Beautification in their hearts is a psychological process, not an explicit identification of relied-on evidence.
alternative: If direct narration resumes, reporter becomes text and scope plain. If the corrective and condemning context is taken to reject the prediction as factually mistaken, truth becomes false. If وَزُيِّنَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ in 48:12 counts as a psychological ground, grounds becomes stated with that clause as evidence.
note: No remembered historical return is used. Attribution and disapproval are clear; truth is kept separate from disapproval.

holder: The Arabs left behind, addressed in the answer to their excuse in 48:11.
proposition: That the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families.
scope_note: وَظَنَنتُمْ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوْءِ is read as a positive restatement within the answer introduced by قُلْ in 48:11. The negative belongs to the earlier proposition restated, not to this attitude.
unsure: proposition: The construction may characterize the preceding nonreturn expectation or add a broader adverse thought whose content is unstated.
reporter: Continuation of instructed speech and resumption of direct narration are possible.
scope: Instructed-speech scope depends on continuing the command from 48:11.
truth: The restatement reading is censured without an explicit narration of return in this window.
grounds: Beautification in their hearts can explain attraction but supplies no explicit relied-on evidence.
alternative: If this adds another adverse thought, the proposition and polarity are unspecified and truth remains open. Resumed narration would change reporter to text and scope to plain. The contextual rejection can support truth=false on the nonreturn reading. Counting وَزُيِّنَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ in 48:12 as a psychological ground makes grounds stated.
note: One unit applies to this verb with its cognate noun; it does not merge this entry with the earlier verb. No remembered historical event supplies the truth value.

holder: The human being of 90:4, depicted as boasting about spending much wealth.
proposition: That no one will have power over him.
scope_note: أَيَحْسَبُ questions the positive attitude; لَّن makes the proposition about power negative. The holder is the general figure ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ of 90:4, with no named individual.
truth_evidence: 90:4 asserts creating the human: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِى كَبَدٍ. 90:20 states the rejecters' fate as عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةٌۢ, presenting power and confinement they cannot escape.
unsure: attitude: The rhetorical question challenges an attitude, without independently asserting that every human holds it.
holder_kind: The general human figure can be narrowed to a boastful type; no particular historical person is identified.
alternative: If only independently asserted attitudes count as held, attitude becomes open. The boastful human can instead be a supposed case, changing holder_kind to hypothetical while retaining generic or hypothetical scope.
note: Additional context requested and read with print-sura: 90:1-20, for the holder and the text's response. Held records the positive attitude under its scopes, not a claim that all humans believe it. The expenditure boast is not explicitly stated as its ground.

holder: The human figure of 90:4 who says in 90:6 that he has spent much wealth.
proposition: That no one has seen him.
scope_note: أَيَحْسَبُ challenges the positive attitude. لَّمْ يَرَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ is the negative proposition, not a denial of thinking. The holder continues the general human figure of 90:4.
unsure: attitude: The rhetorical question can be left open as an assertion about what the figure actually believes.
holder_kind: The figure can be generic or a supposed boastful type.
truth: The rebuking question does not explicitly name who saw him; the gift of eyes is not itself a direct assertion that he was seen.
proposition: No specific occasion is expressed; connection to his preceding boast is plausible but not explicit.
alternative: The sequence, especially أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عَيْنَيْنِ in 90:8, can imply that the maker of his faculties sees him; then truth becomes false. Restricting held to independent assertion makes attitude open; a supposed type makes holder_kind hypothetical.
note: Additional context requested and read with print-sura: 90:1-20, for the antecedent and surrounding response. No spender, expenditure event, or observer is supplied from memory. Held records the positive attitude placed under questioning.

holder: Those who have done wrong, considered at the day of resurrection.
proposition: That evil consequences of their deeds and the punishment they mocked would appear to them from God.
scope_note: لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ negates their prior expectation, without making the expected proposition negative. لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ names a class at judgment. I read وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ as a fresh assertion after the counterfactual ransom introduced by وَلَوْ, so the attitude is not itself conditional.
truth_evidence: 39:47 asserts وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ. 39:48 expands this with وَبَدَا لَهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا كَسَبُوا۟ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ.
unsure: scope: The appearing clause may be coordinated within the conditional consequence instead of being an independent assertion.
holder_kind: The class may refer specifically to the group disbelieving in the hereafter in 39:45.
proposition: 39:47 leaves the relative object unspecified; the concrete description comes from its continuation in 39:48.
alternative: If the appearing clause is within the consequence of the counterfactual ransom, scope additionally includes conditional. If the holder is specifically the group of 39:45, holder_kind becomes specific and generic or hypothetical can be removed unless retained for the counterfactual case.
note: I take the third-person account in 39:47 as resumed narration after the instructed prayer addressing God as You in 39:46. The unexpected thing occurs; the negation concerns their previous expectation. No basis for the prior failure to expect it is reported.
